nj_bouldering_northeast_nj.blurb: Northeast New Jersey bouldering is a scattering of small areas within an hour's drive of New York City, across the Ramapo, Watchung and Palisades ridges. The rock changes with the ridge: basalt and gabbro in the Watchungs, diabase on the Palisades, granite and gneiss in the Ramapos. Nearly all of it is bouldering, with problems from very easy to V10, most of them between V0 and V4 and a smaller group of harder ones. The largest collections are at South Mountain Reservation, Garrett Mountain, Cedar Grove Reservoir and the Ramapo bouldering. Garrett Mountain is a cliff line overlooking Paterson, with a cluster of flakes, aretes and a splitter crack below a tower. Finding the good problems takes some local knowledge.

mt_big_belt_mountains.blurb: The Big Belt Mountains lie east of Canyon Ferry Reservoir near Helena, Montana, with climbing gathered in a few canyons: Avalanche Gulch, Hellgate Gulch, Beaver Creek and Trout Creek Canyon. The canyon walls hold plenty of limestone, pocketed and sometimes crumbly, so nearly everything is bolted and trad is a small share. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.13, with 5.10 the biggest slice and a solid group of 5.12s. Climbing is possible most of the year. Hellgate is the sunnier of the two busiest gulches, and its Winter Wall is pleasant on sunny winter days, while upper Beaver and Trout Creeks offer shade in summer and a quieter day out. Wear a helmet in spring, when freeze-thaw loosens rock.

nm_aguirre_bouldering.blurb: Aguirre Bouldering is scattered across the east side of the Organ Mountains near Las Cruces, New Mexico, where the range rises in a wall of needle-like spires above Chihuahuan Desert and looks out over the Tularosa Basin. The problems are spread out, often a handful or up to a dozen on one block, and some boulders sit close to the road while others need a longer walk. Everything here is bouldering, from very easy to V8, with the bulk between V0 and V5. Boulder 36, Snake Den, Cactararium and the NIMBY Boulder are among the larger groupings. Across the Organs as a whole, desert sun matters year-round, with sunny walls favored in winter and shadier ones in summer.

wa_smithbrook.blurb: Smithbrook is a spread of forest bouldering in Washington's Central-East Cascades, reached from Highway 2. Everything here is bouldering, with problems from V0 up to V12, most of them between V1 and V5 and a real group of harder lines above V8. Blockbuster Boulders is the largest zone, a collection of boulders in the woods with a good number of strong lines. Lichtenberg Boulders sits beneath a big slab on Lichtenberg Mountain, a longer hike in that sees few other boulderers, with summer bugs and humidity much like the neighboring Treasury. Outer Space Boulders and the 2nd Talus are other sizable pockets.

wa_southwest_cascades.blurb: The Southwest Cascades are volcano country in southern Washington, home to Mount Rainier and Mount Adams, the state's two highest peaks, along with scrambling and high meadows in the Tatoosh Range and Goat Rocks. The terrain is gentler than the North Cascades, with forested peaks and meadows, and the big volcanoes are lava rock rather than granite. Sport climbing is the largest single share, with crags such as Pinto Rock and Monte Cristo Slab, mostly at easy to moderate grades up to the low 5.11s. Mountaineering and alpine routes on Rainier and Adams add glacier and snow climbing, with some ice, scrambling from class 2 to 4, and a bit of trad and bouldering. Rainier is known for iconic glacier climbs.
